Thank you, Madam Chair. Good morning, everyone. My name is Angela Crook, Integrity Commissioner for the City of Saskatoon.
It is my pleasure today to present to the Governance and Priorities Committee, the annual report for the Integrity Commissioner covering the calendar year of 2024.
There are several functions covered by the role of Integrity Commissioner. In 2024, there were three areas that I was called upon to perform.
The Services Education and Complaints. The advisory function performed by the Integrity Commissioner involves responding to members of Council on questions of compliance with the Code of Ethics.
In 2024, I received one request, provide an advance ruling from a member of Council that related to the section on the acceptance of gifts and benefits.
Complaints can be categorized as formal and informal.

Complaints or inquiries are just concerns of some sort raised by people. Sometimes the informal complaints are related to conduct that's covered by the Code of Ethics and sometimes they are entirely unrelated.
Either way, I respond to each informal complaint that's made to my office. In 2024, I received five informal complaints or inquiries, all of which came from members of the public.
And this number of inquiries is pretty typical for the City of Saskatoon over the last three years.
Formal complaints are a request that an investigation be performed into the conduct of a member of Council and they must comply with the criteria in the Code.
In 2024, I received 14 formal complaints. Three of which were investigated, but there were no violations of the Code of Ethics found.
So even though the number of formal complaints increased pretty substantially in 2024, when you look behind the data, the numbers tell us slightly different story.
Four of the complaints in 2024 related to conduct during the election campaign, and when the member of Council wasn't reelected, there was no jurisdiction for those complaints to continue.
Six of the complaints were found to be vexatious and filed in bad slate faith, and therefore were not investigated any further.
A finding of bad faith is relatively rare with integrity commissioner decisions, at least from the ones that I can tell that are reported publicly.
The motivation for filing a complaint is generally not a critical factor if the complaint contains some sort of minimum level of merit.
In this case, I found that six complaints submitted by the same complainant had a dishonest motive and very, very limited merit.
Therefore, leading to a decision of Vexatious complaints or bad faith.
This investigation report confirmed for me that the Code of Ethics has appropriate mechanisms in place to prevent the so-called weaponization against members of Council.
There was also one complaint from 2023 that was reported on in my 2024 annual report, which is when the investigation concluded.
This complaint resulted in a finding that a member of Council violated the respect section of the Code of Ethics during a telephone conversation with a constituent.
The full investigation report related to this complaint was made public when it was presented to Council in June of 2020.

In 2024, I met virtually with other integrity commissioners from Manitoba, Alberta and British Columbia, where we had a series of roundtable discussions on a variety of topics that are relevant in all four of the Western provinces.
Out of these meetings two things became very clear to me.
One is that although there are a variety of different ethics bylaws in place in these provinces, there are also many commonalities to the structures in place for the Code of Ethics.
The second thing that became clear to me is that the issues facing integrity commissioners and municipal councils in terms of ethics are not unique in any of the provinces.
There was a lot of commonality.
There was a commitment from all of the integrity commissioners that attended these meetings to continue these meetings and to plan for a more in depth conference, hopefully in 2025.
In closing, I would like to thank everyone in administration members of Council and members of the public that I have worked with over the last year.
Everyone has been very cooperative and easy to work with, which makes the investigation process more efficient and effective.
